name: Epcot Thrill Rides
intro: Epcot spent its first three decades as the Disney park you visited for the food and the ambiance — thrills were optional. That changed fast. Between Guardians, Test Track 3.0, and Mission: SPACE's Orange Mission, it now has a legitimate lineup for guests who want their pulse to move. These are the rides that give Epcot its edge.

rides.blurb: The anchor of the collection and the ride that changed the conversation about Epcot — a fully enclosed reverse-launch coaster with a killer playlist is not something anyone expected to find here.
The park's speed benchmark — 65 mph around the outside of the pavilion, now dressed in retro-futurist GM styling for version 3.0.
Orange Mission produces real G-forces via centrifuge — the closest thing to legitimate astronaut training at any Disney park, and it belongs here on physical merits alone.
Not a thrill ride by any traditional definition, but being lifted 40 feet over an 80-foot IMAX dome earns it a spot — the Grand Canyon stomach-drop is real.
The lightest entry here, but it moves faster and with more purpose than you'd expect from a Frozen boat ride. Worth revisiting after the 2026 animatronic upgrade.
